Responsibilites:

Make sure he's not TOO nervous on wedding day... I brought a PS3 and a couple of games he like to play while we were waiting for the ceremony began. This got him talking, and not focusing on being nervous. He's supposed to enjoy himself, not have a heart attack.

You're in charge of the rings... DON'T LOSE THEM! This falls into the above paragraph.

If there are any last-minute "disasters," try to be the one who reassures the groom it's all going to be fine, and try to take care of it without involving the groom... Again, falls into that first paragraph.

As for a stripper-less bachelor party, it's all dependent on the groom's tastes. For one wedding, I got the other groomsmen together and we set up a camping trip with some whitewater rafting for the groom. We all paid our own ways, and we spilt the cost of the groom... He didn't pay a dime.

Just do something that he'll enjoy. Remember (first paragraph), he's going to be nervous about the whole thing. Get him out of his head and get him to have fun. This is the most important point to remember.

You and the bridesmaid are the wedding day managers - the bride and groom want to enjoy the day not deal with all the little things that come up. Understand the wedding plan from the bride and groom, get everyone where they need to be, ring and paperwork, handle spats with the relatives, and make sure the pastor and banquet hall get paid.

For the bachelor party - make sure the groom gets to the wedding alive. That's all you have to do.

Compared to the maid of honor, best men really have it easy. At the weddings I've been in, they help to keep the groomsmen informed of the schedule and make sure that they're at the right place at the right time wearing the right thing. This will help the bride and groom immensely depending on the groomsmen. If you want to really be awesome, asking what you can do to help a day or two before the wedding would be incredibly helpful. Volunteering to help set up tables and chairs, fold napkins, set up the backdrop for the ceremony are all things that would help take some stress off of the couple. Bonus points for recruiting your fellow groomsmen, if necessary.

In addition to this, best men are also responsible for planning the bachelor party (which it seems like you're aware of already), holding the rings, being a witness for the signing of the marriage documents, giving the appropriate checks to various vendors following the ceremony, and traditionally giving a toast at the reception. Also, the best man often is the one responsible for turning in all the tuxes after the wedding, especially if the bride and groom are leaving immediately after the wedding for their honeymoon.

When I was the best man for my friend's wedding, we went to a brewery/restaurant that had really good food, then walked to a hookah bar because he loves to smoke hookah.

It's important that the groom not pay for anything at his bachelor party (weddings are expensive enough), so the best man should coordinate with the other groomsmen and guests to pay for the bachelor's meals and drinks and so forth. Most restaurants will divide the check up for you, so each person can pay a little bit extra and it doesn't get expensive for anybody.

At the wedding, you stand wherever they tell you and do whatever you're told. The couple will usually have you hold on to the rings during the ceremony. If there is a ring bearer, make sure he knows what to do. Usually you will keep the real rings and the ring bearer will have fake ones, but if the couple really wants the ring bearer to use the real rings, watch him (and the pillow) like a hawk until he hands them off to you. The couple will often ask you to be a witness to the marriage, so you might be signing the marriage certificate (write neatly). Always be prepared to pose for lots of pictures.

At the reception, you give a little speech. Play to your strengths as a public speaker and always keep it short and not too embarrassing. You're also in charge of keeping the other groomsmen and ushers in line during the ceremony and reception. Make sure the groom (and sometimes the other guests) doesn't get too drunk or raucous at the reception and ensure that nobody home drives drunk, especially the couple themselves. It's fine if you drink a little and have sex as long as you stay safe (use protection and don't drive drunk) and don't abandon the couple somewhere.

Always be encouraging (but honest) with the groom. You'll probably have to deal with the maid of honor quite a bit and take some pictures with her, so be ready for that. She is in charge of the ladies, but you might have to assist her on occasion.

And don't let anybody kidnap the bride.
